name: Slow Cooker Maple Dijon Pork Bowls
intro_html: Three main ingredients, one slow cooker, and dinner is basically done. Sugar-free maple syrup and dijon mustard glaze lean pork tenderloin until it is tender and just a little sweet, served over potatoes with green beans. It runs around ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) and gives you {{protein}} grams of protein across 14 bowls.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Sugar-Free Maple Syrup, 1/2 cup: ~$0.47. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (garlic powder, salt, black pepper): ~$0.25. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $37.81 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.70 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $40.03 across 14 servings, roughly $2.86 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.35 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $46.38. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Sugar-free maple syrup keeps this glaze sweet without the sugar hit. Buy one bottle of sugar-free syrup and it lasts through many batches.
Frozen green beans cost less than fresh and never spoil on you. Keep bags of frozen green beans on hand for meals like this.
A ten pound bag of potatoes is the cheapest way to buy them. Buy the big potato bag and you will use every last one.
make_it: Season the pork tenderloin with the salt and pepper, then place it in the slow cooker.
Stir the sugar-free maple syrup, dijon mustard, and garlic powder together, then pour it over the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is fork tender.
Steam the green beans just until crisp-tender near the end.
Roast or boil the potatoes until soft.
Slice or shred the pork, serve it over potatoes, and add the green beans on the side.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings comes in at {{protein}} grams of protein and just {{cal}} calories.
